title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference: September 21, 2026
headline: Cardinals' downfield passing game stalled (0 completions over 10 yards) but LaFleur defends Marvin Harrison Jr., says Trey McBride and Bourne handle underneath work, and CB Will Johnson may miss the season with a neck injury.
summary: LaFleur said the offense couldn't connect downfield against Seattle, with no completions over 10 yards and only four attempts. He blamed his own play-calling timing, protection leaks, and imprecise drop steps and transitions, and said the second half had no rhythm 'starting with me.' Seattle played a lot of shell coverage and gave up checkdowns, and the offense failed to convert third-and-manageable situations. He defended Marvin Harrison Jr., rejecting the effort criticism and saying the misses were about protection, coverage, and self-inflicted errors. He said Trey McBride and Kendrick Bourne handle the underneath work and that roles are set, though that could change this week. On the run game, he said mid zone has been pretty good, duo needs work, and Jeremiyah Love had some good moments but also a lack of clarity on a first-and-goal play. He praised Gardner Minshew's... actually Jacoby Brissett's command and distribution against pressure, and the line's protection plan. On injuries, Max Melton is day to day, and Will Johnson has a neck injury that could cost him the whole season, though surgery isn't expected. The team looks ahead to a Sunday 1:00 game at Levi's Stadium.

injuries.detail: Day to day; LaFleur said more will be known Wednesday or Thursday.
Neck injury that could cost him the entire season; LaFleur doesn't believe surgery is needed but isn't certain.

signals.note: He is used as a deep and backside option and the offense struggled to connect, so his volume is real but efficiency is shaky.

signals.note: He is the designated underneath weapon, and with deep shots failing, he should see a steady target floor.

signals.note: He has a modest underneath role, with limited upside unless the offense changes.
signals.quote: you got Kendrick who works underneath pretty well too.

signals.note: He had some good moments but also a lack of clarity on a first-and-goal; the run game needs to be cleaner for him to produce consistently.
signals.quote: I thought Jeremiah had the two right there

signals.claim: Brissett is the starting quarterback and handled pressure well.
signals.note: The coach praised his command and distribution, so his job looks secure even as the offense struggles.

signals.claim: Johnson could miss the whole season with a neck injury.
signals.note: Cardinals' cornerback depth takes a hit; relevant for IDP and matchups against Arizona's secondary.
signals.quote: potentially could miss the whole season, so. Yeah. Sucks for him, obviously.

signals.claim: Melton's availability will be clearer Wednesday or Thursday.
signals.note: Another corner in question, further thinning the secondary.
signals.quote: we're going to kind of be a little bit more day to day

topics.detail: LaFleur said you can't dink and dunk against top defenses and need explosives, but Seattle's shell coverages made it hard. He took blame for timing of shot calls and short-yardage calls.
Mid zone has been pretty good, duo needs to improve, and a misaligned defense on one play led to a missed opportunity because there was no check built into the call.
LaFleur praised the defense's goal-line stands and fight on the last drive but said they were on the field too much in the second half.
Starling is still working back from injury and is in a good spot physically and mentally, with LaFleur saying he has played good football.
LaFleur praised Burch as flashing on special teams and defense, saying he can be as good as he wants to be.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 3 Media Availability | Monday, September 21st | Press Conference
headline: Stefanski won't name a Thursday QB (Penix reportedly trending to start; Tua 'getting better'), and he downplayed Kyle Pitts' season-low snaps as a game-flow result, not a plan.
summary: Stefanski opened by laying out the short-week schedule for Thursday night at Green Bay: lifting and meetings Monday, a quick practice Tuesday, and a walk-through Wednesday before the team flies out. He declined to name a starting quarterback, saying he has a decent idea but wants to talk to the players first and may update later today. He would not comment on reports that Michael Penix Jr. is trending toward starting, but said he talks to Penix daily and is very confident in those discussions and in the medical process. Tua Tagovailoa is 'getting better,' though what that means for this week is undetermined. On injuries, many MRIs are pending and he had no major updates, with an estimated injury report due after the walk-through. He called the offense's production through two games 'not good enough' in every area, put the blame on coaches as well, and said he is confident in the scheme and the run-game plan. Kyle Pitts' lowest-ever snap share was blamed on the second half getting away from them, and Stefanski said Pitts remains a big part of the plan. He said Drake London must be a pro after the fan incident and that London took accountability, and he stressed that turnover margin and complementary football are the main points of emphasis. Cooper Rush was pulled for Jack Strand in-game because it was 'best for the football team,' and he praised Strand's development.

injuries.detail: Stefanski wouldn't say whether Penix will play Thursday; he is in daily contact with Penix and the medical staff and is very confident in those discussions. A decision comes after he talks to the players.
Described as 'getting better'; what that means for this week is still being worked through.

signals.note: Rush was benched amid fan booing and poor offense, so his hold on the starting job looks tenuous.
signals.quote: I'm just constantly trying to do what's best for the football team.

signals.note: He is the emergency QB depth, but the praise was about development, not a role change.
signals.quote: I'm very excited about Jack's development and, and the work that he's putting in

signals.note: With only one catch so far, a rebound is plausible if the offense has more balance, but there is no concrete target commitment.
signals.quote: Kyle's a big part of what we do.

signals.note: No discipline or role change was mentioned, so it's a minor off-field note.
signals.quote: He has to be a pro.

signals.claim: Stefanski didn't commit to more Bijan touches but said the run game needs to be fixed and the offense needs more balance.
signals.note: A fourth-down jet sweep to London instead of Bijan was questioned, and the coach offered no clarity, so expect a run-game focus that might help Bijan's volume.

topics.detail: Stefanski said the offense is not good enough in any area after two games, with coaches sharing the blame. He expressed frustration but said the staff must find solutions, and he believes in the scheme and players.
His main message to the team was to fix the turnover margin, take care of the ball, create takeaways, and win the field-position game.
He is confident in the run-game plan but said it must be judged holistically, and more offensive balance would help every facet.
The team wants explosive plays and has missed on deep shots to Pitts and Dotson in the first two games, but he said you have to take your shots when the defense allows.
He called Green Bay's offense efficient and explosive through the pass game, praised Jordan Love's arm talent and ability to win in and outside the pocket, and called Watson a big-play target.

title: Jesse Minter Reflects on Ravens' Week 2 Performance
headline: Ravens look to get Flowers, Stanley and Madubuike back for Dallas in Rio. Bateman and Andrews stepped up in Flowers' absence. Trenton Simpson is playing at a high level, though Teddye Buchanan's return could change his role.
summary: Minter opened by saying the team is looking inward after the Week 2 loss to the Saints. He said the Ravens had chances in all three phases to break the game open or finish it and didn't. He explained the third-and-one decision: the previous play was really a 1.5-to-2-yard situation, and he did not want to risk giving New Orleans the ball at the plus-36 in a tie game, so he went to a punt rather than a Derrick Henry run. He said Henry was 'definitely himself' with nothing significant wrong. He was critical of the special teams (a late block operation, a kick return he thought the team misread) and the defense's third-down tackling, and he called out operational and defensive penalties as a major emphasis. On health, he said the team should have a good shot at getting a lot of the dinged-up players back this week, with more clarity Wednesday. He praised Rashod Bateman and Mark Andrews for stepping up with a key player missing. He said Trenton Simpson is playing like one of the team's best players even with Teddye Buchanan hopefully returning. He expressed confidence in Malaki Starks after a rough game. The team practices normally Wednesday and flies to Brazil Thursday evening to face the Cowboys.

topics.detail: Minter said the previous play was closer to 1.5-2 yards. After the incompletion he chose to punt rather than risk giving the Saints the ball at the plus-36 in a tie game, and he said he doesn't believe in second-guessing the call. He said he talked with Declan about it.

A field goal was blocked after the operation was about half a second late. On the second-quarter kickoff, he regretted not trusting his kickoff team to knock the ball down. The Saints took a short field with three timeouts and 25 seconds left and the kickoff coverage misread the return.

Third-and-long breakdowns included poor leverage on the flat, an unabated four-man rush, and coverage lost on a scramble. He wants better tackling of check-downs, better angles, and faster, more decisive play. The defense gave up three points on a third quarter drive.

Operational penalties on offense (not getting set, receiver moving his feet on quick snaps) and defensive penalties like roughing the passer, plus a holding on a two-point try, are a major emphasis. He rejected 'new offense' as an excuse.

A player Minter called 'Cheeto' (name unclear in captions) saw only one snap. Minter said he wants to get him on the field more, especially on defense. On offense he was a fifth receiver in a reserve role because of multiple-tight-end sets and few second-half possessions.

Normal Wednesday practice, flight Thursday evening, arrival Friday morning with a focus on recovery and a normal Friday work session. Minter said the field condition is in the league's hands and he feels pretty good about it.

title: Dave Canales breaks down Panthers' defensive response and Bryce Young's progress
headline: Jonathon Brooks' groin injury is still being evaluated with updates held until Wednesday, while Bryce Young and the downfield passing game are trending up and Pat Jones is optimistic to return.
summary: Coach Canales praised the complementary football in the win over Atlanta. Special teams field position (about a 220-yard starting-drive edge) and defensive turnovers drove the result, and tackling improved from Week 1. Run defense is still not where he wants it, and offensive penalties made it hard to establish the run game. Offensively he liked the explosive plays and Bryce Young's distribution, but he flagged going 3-for-6 on red zone trips and wants a more balanced approach on early downs to avoid known passing situations. Jonathon Brooks is getting extensive imaging on a groin issue, and Canales will say nothing more until Wednesday. Pat Jones was close to playing but was held out after a setback in how he responded to Friday's workload, though Canales is optimistic about this week. Young's downfield aggression was described as by design, with growth coming from ownership, anticipation and chemistry with Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, Xavier Legette, the tight ends and newly arrived Darren Waller. Defensively he highlighted Devin Lloyd's two interceptions, Jaelan Phillips' sack, Bobby Okereke's near-interceptions, Lee Hunter's play inside, and contributions from the rookies. Coker will keep returning kicks for now despite an ankle issue that the team wants to manage.

title: Ben Johnson recaps loss to Vikings, looks ahead to Monday Night Football vs. Eagles | Press Conference
headline: Caleb Williams is week to week and unlikely to practice this week, so Tyson Bagent is the likely starter for Monday night vs. the Eagles, though Johnson has not ruled Williams out.
summary: Johnson said the film review matched his view from the night before: the Bears had plenty of chances to beat the Vikings, with all three phases making game-changing plays, but they didn't capitalize. Caleb Williams is week to week, and Johnson called the medical report "somewhat encouraging." He doesn't believe Williams will practice this week but declined to rule him out for Week 3, and he refused to put a timeline on the recovery. Johnson expressed strong confidence in Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum if a quarterback change is needed, citing a year and a half of work together and game experience. He blamed the offense's struggles against Minnesota's defense on penalties and third-and-long situations, noting the offense improved in the second half with no penalties and three red-zone trips. He was disappointed in the execution on the three snaps from the 12 at the end of the game, and the Bears scored zero points on their three second-half red-zone chances. He would not detail the blocking scheme on the final play, which involved Colston Loveland. He also said the field goal operation was not clean, citing a high snap and a block off the edge that wasn't fixed after the first warning.

injuries.detail: Listed week to week. Johnson doesn't expect him to practice this week but did not rule him out for Week 3, and he gave no timeline. He called the medical report somewhat encouraging and said Williams recovers faster than most.

signals.note: Bagent becomes the likely starter if Williams sits, and Johnson says he can run the offense.
signals.quote: I feel strongly about what he's capable of.

A high snap and a poor operation led to a blocked field goal. Johnson called the first field goal a warning shot, and the second was blocked off the edge because the problem wasn't fixed in time.
All three quarterbacks improved from year one to year two, based on charted throws in camp. Johnson described the room as cerebral and competitive and said it has three players who can win games.

title: Zac Taylor: "We're Not A Finished Product" | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Bengals are 2-0 and Taylor is happy with the run game, with Chase Brown singled out. He sees explosive runs close, praises Burrow, Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase, and notes the defensive line depth.
summary: Taylor was pleased with how the defense, offense and special teams complemented each other in the road win. The defense held the opposing backs to 14 carries for 18 yards, pressured the quarterback, and got a key fourth-and-one stop. He said the offense was held back by pre-snap penalties (false start, hold, snap issue) that created long-yardage situations, and that his team will correct them. He praised Joe Burrow's pocket movement and ball security and said Burrow is already at the point of creating plays this early in the season. He highlighted Ja'Marr Chase's touchdown catch, Tee Higgins' crossing-route throw, and Chase Brown's tough finishing runs. He said the run game is close to breaking explosive plays, one block or one communication away, even though the yardage totals looked modest. He praised the pass-rush depth, especially Cedric Johnson and rookie Cashius Howell, and noted Dexter Lawrence's coverage drops. Pittsburgh on the road is the sole focus, and he called it a grimy divisional game where turnovers, field position and penalties will decide the outcome.

Pre-snap penalties put the offense in long-yardage situations early, and he wants those cleaned up. He was fine with the run-heavy tendencies from under center because the game script allowed it.
The run game is producing eight- and nine-yard carries, and Taylor believes it is a block or a communication away from home runs. He said that is what turns an 80-yard rushing day into 140.
Taylor said 'we're not a finished product' and that the team is focused on finding wins and taking care of the ball. Cincinnati is one of four 2-0 AFC teams.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference: September 21st, 2026
headline: Watson (offensive player of game) keeps the QB job with his legs a real weapon, but the run game is bad (65 ypg), Judkins' carries should rise once it improves, Jeudy's targets are capped, and Tyson Campbell's status is uncertain.
summary: Monken, coming off his first win as a head coach, called the 65-yard-per-game rushing average a fact and said the staff must scheme, coach, call and block it better. The offense pivoted to quick throws and getting the ball in space because opponents pressured them on under-center play action. He praised Deshaun Watson for using his legs (a design run, a scramble, and a naked bootleg dump to Harold Fannin), named him offensive player of the game, and expects continued growth because he has been out of football a while and is learning a new system. He denied any real conflict with Watson, calling the back-and-forth healthy. On defense, he said Carson Schwesinger, who missed much of camp, played much better and was defensive player of the game, Mason Graham played better, and Myles Harden bounced back with an interception. He explained that Jerry Jeudy's targets are limited because there is only one football and the run game struggled, and said Quinshon Judkins will get more carries as the run game improves. Tyson Campbell warmed up but did not play, is dealing with several issues, and Monken likes his chances to play this week. He defended an aggressive fourth-and-inches call on Judkins after a botched sneak and a lost challenge.

injuries.detail: Dealing with a number of things (including a previously known ankle issue); warmed up but did not play after the delay. Monken likes his chances to play based on how he's wired, and will see how the week goes.

signals.note: Starter with rushing upside and the coach's backing; he was named offensive player of the game.

signals.note: Volume is tied to fixing a struggling ground game, so the upside is conditional.

signals.note: Target share is capped by competition from Fannin and the rookies, and Monken offered no firm commitment.
signals.quote: Jerry's opportunities will come.

signals.note: Named among the options competing with Jeudy for targets, which keeps his role steady.
signals.quote: he dumped it down to Harold for a first down.

signals.note: He scored a touchdown on a play Watson changed at the line, which shows trust and a growing connection.
signals.quote: their mindset and their competitiveness and their attention to detail separates them.

signals.claim: Concepcion is a featured receiver in the offense along with Boston.
signals.note: Monken praised him as one of two rookies who are special and keep drawing targets.
signals.quote: Their skill set might be different, but their mindset is, is the same.

signals.note: A starting CB with an uncertain status is relevant for matchups against opposing WRs.
signals.quote: I like his chances to be able to play based on how he's wired.

signals.claim: Schwesinger has shaken off the missed training camp and played much better.
signals.note: Defensive player of the game and a strong IDP option going forward.
signals.quote: He was defensive player of the game this week.

signals.claim: Graham will keep improving as an interior pass rusher.
signals.note: He is producing pressure from the interior and is a rising IDP.

signals.claim: Harden bounced back after Week 1 with an interception and another big play in the end zone.
signals.note: Positive for IDP and for his role in the secondary.
signals.quote: he had a great week of practice.

topics.detail: Monken says the 65 yards per game average is unacceptable and blames scheme, play calling, coaching and blocking. The offense relied on quick throws against pressure, and lost-yardage plays and penalties put them behind the sticks.
Monken stood by going for it on fourth-and-inches with Judkins after a botched sneak, and said he'll remain aggressive. He also admitted the challenge was wrong but doesn't regret it.
The offense's operation was cleaner with practice modifications. Some wristband calls are being shortened, and Watson has freedom to change plays at the line.
Monken downplayed any back-and-forth with Watson, calling the exchanges healthy, and said splitting reps in the quarterback competition didn't help the eventual starter.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: Postgame Week 2 #WASvsDAL
headline: Dallas leaned pass-heavy by design in a 37-20 win (66 rush yards), with Dak, CeeDee and Pickens clicking; PJ Locke (foot) and Cobie Durant (hamstring) are banged up and Barham had a stinger.
summary: Schottenheimer said the plan was to throw the ball around and use play-action, so the ugly 66 rushing yards were partly intentional. He praised the passing game as hitting on all cylinders, singling out the Dak Prescott-CeeDee Lamb connection, tough catches by George Pickens, and touchdowns from Ryan Flournoy and Jake Ferguson. Dak was celebrated for breaking the franchise passing record, with the coach calling his preparation abnormal and his work ethic unique. Defensively he saw better communication and red-zone play, a won turnover margin and a big fourth-down stop, but said third down and containing the QB on scrambles still need cleanup. Rookie Jaishawn Barham handled the green-dot role, with Shemar James rotating in on certain packages, though Barham had a couple of stingers. Injuries: P.J. Locke (foot) and Cobie Durant (hamstring, needs more tests) were hurt, and Barham had a stinger but returned. Next is a Brazil game with an unusual week, and he said he is not concerned about the field. He also wants to get KaVontae Turpin more involved on offense and said Brandon Aubrey's long field goals are a major weapon.

title: HC Sean Payton on Broncos’ win over Jaguars: ‘It was really a tale of two halves’
headline: Jaylen Waddle had a breakout 8-138 game and Sean Payton praised him heavily; RJ Harvey is out and J.K. Dobbins has a hamstring issue, so rookie Jonah Coleman stepped into the backfield.
summary: Payton described the 20-13 win over Jacksonville as a tale of two halves. Denver moved the ball in the first half but failed to finish drives, then played much more consistently after halftime. He called the defense's response good, citing third-down stops and a big takeaway, and said the game felt like what he expects from this team after last week's rough Monday night loss. Waddle was the standout: Payton called his impact significant, pointed to his explosiveness and run after the catch, and attributed the production to a mix of matchups (slot or Z alignments, man looks against a zone-heavy team) and a healthier snap count and possession total than in Week 1. The backfield was thin, with Harvey out and Dobbins hurt, leaving only two backs plus the fullback. Rookie Jonah Coleman scored a touchdown and played well on the final drive, and Payton said it didn't look like a rookie series. Payton said Denver made a concerted effort to run more, leaning on the offensive line and more under-center work to take pressure off the quarterback. Dobbins is frustrated and has a hamstring problem, and his status is unresolved.

title: Campbell on perspective and improving
headline: Avonte Maddox is done for the season, so Detroit's secondary is in flux. Branch is out for Week 3, and Campbell is adding veteran and young safeties and says more defenders will get playing time.
summary: Campbell opened by saying Avonte Maddox needs surgery and will miss the rest of the season. He then spent most of the session on the 1-1 team's fundamentals and urgency heading into Week 3. His main complaints were third and fourth down conversions on both sides, an inconsistent run game and defense, too few explosive plays, red zone and goal-line failures, 18 penalties (14 he called unacceptable), and special teams punt coverage. Detroit has been aggressive on first down and leads the league in forcing second-and-7-plus, but opponents are converting about 66% on later downs, which he blames on breakdowns in trust and discipline. He said the Lions are bringing in veteran DBs and possibly young safeties from other teams, and that the defense will move players around and give more snaps to players who have earned them. Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph will not practice or play this week, with Branch likely back before Joseph, whose knee is still being strengthened after a stretch without full work. Healthy scratches Ennis Rakestraw and another young defender could get looks, and Campbell said he is open to everything. On offense he said that in hindsight they might have thrown more early after running stalled the first two drives against Buffalo. He backed defensive coordinator Shep Sheppard, said the team won't know its identity until around the bye, and said he is not discouraged. The next opponent is the Jets under Aaron Glenn.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Building Toward the Colts Matchup | Full Q&A
headline: Nico Collins has no update yet, C.J. Stroud's limp is unchecked, and Jaylin Noel's growing role comes with a promise to use the tight ends more after the 0-2 start.

He defended the decision to kick a 58-yard field goal and the fourth-and-1 call. He said the play failed because the line didn't double-team Dexter Lawrence, and he made clear the failure wasn't on rookie guard Keylan Rutledge alone. He gave the Bengals' defensive line credit for shutting down the run and said the team must stay committed to it, mixing outside zone and gap schemes. He said the offense can use its tight ends more. Game flow pushed them into more 11 personnel than planned, even though they prepared multiple-tight-end sets. He praised Jaylin Noel's explosive plays, jet sweep work and improved punt returning, and said his role will keep developing. Nico Collins had no update because he is still rehabbing, and Ryans hadn't seen C.J. Stroud after the limp reported at Stroud's press conference. The defense improved on week one, with better effort and a pass rush that affected the quarterback, but it needs to play better on third downs and keep points off the board. Ryans called the Colts game as important as any other and said the message to the team is to stay connected and finish games.

title: Liam Coen Recaps Loss to the Broncos | Press Conference
headline: Jaguars lost 20-13 to Denver after a second-half collapse. Coen says Travis Hunter needs more looks, and the offense was out of sync with Lawrence under pressure.
summary: Coen took responsibility for the 20-13 loss, saying the team did not coach, play or finish well enough in all three phases after halftime. He called the field goal on the first drive out of the half a missed chance to go up two scores. The offense stalled after an explosive pass to Jakobi Meyers, and a field goal was missed. He said the offense was out of sync late, with the ball coming out earlier than planned because of pressure, and he was frustrated by drops and missed one-on-one chances. Protection was a problem: he felt the quarterback took too many hits and probably forced a throw into a cloud-coverage look that was picked off underneath. Denver mixed coverages enough that dinking and dunking was not going to work, so Jacksonville stayed with its plan. He said they will look for more ways to get Travis Hunter targets. On defense, the pass rush was not good enough. Denver picked up blitzes it identified pre-snap, and Coen said they will have to create more pressure and finish when they do blitz. He said the defensive rotation is the same plan used the week before, and he insisted he stayed aggressive on offense with a 10-point lead.

title: Head Coach Jim Harbaugh Postgame Press Conference vs. Raiders

headline: Patriots O-line and safety depth are thin after injuries to Dre'Mont Jones and Dell Pettus. Drake Maye's decision-making and pocket play were criticized, and the run game was called inconsistent. Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas drew praise with A.J. Brown out.
summary: Vrabel said Dre'Mont Jones didn't finish the game and that the team will wait to see how he progresses. He later said he doesn't expect a player to be available for the next few weeks, though the transcript doesn't make clear who he meant. He said the safety room took a double hit, with Dell Pettus out with an ankle injury, and that veteran practice squad players, including Mike Brown, will factor in this week. Up front, Greg Van Roten stepped in and had some good plays and some he'd like back. Caleb Lomu could be an option inside, but he has mostly practiced at tackle. Vrabel was frank about the offense, saying Drake Maye should have dumped the interception down to Reggie Gilliam and that he could have manipulated the pocket better. He also said blocking needs to be more consistent, and Jared Wilson had a down game. He praised the receivers' decisions and catching with A.J. Brown out, and singled out DeMario Douglas's blocking and Kyle Williams's third-down conversion. He said the run game had some positive runs and some that 'stunk', and that offensive identity doesn't have to come from the run. Defensively he praised Gabe Jacas's coachability and the activity of Robert Spillane and Elliott Davison. He said the defense's identity is affecting the quarterback and creating turnovers.

title: Kellen Moore recaps win over Ravens 9/21/2026
headline: Left tackle Kelvin Banks needs ankle surgery and may be out for the season, so Asim Richards steps in. Pete Werner and Tyler Shough drew praise, and Martin Emerson Jr. (shoulder) is day to day.
summary: Moore called the Week 2 win over the Ravens a good, resilient team effort, but said the team is nowhere close to where it needs to be. Kelvin Banks will have ankle surgery in the next few days, and Moore left the door open to a return this season without giving a timeline. Asim Richards takes over the snaps, and Moore called him steady, said he held his own in pass pro, and noted that playing next to David Edwards should help. Moore praised Pete Werner's 11 tackles, sack, urgency and decisiveness. He also highlighted Juwan Johnson's third-and-eight run-after-catch and Tyler Shough's toughness against pressure. On the run game, he saw good cutback and cross runs and good blocking from Edwards, but too many negative runs. He said the team needs to coach and execute better, and that the offense has stalled on second and third down for two straight games. Moore described the Alvin Kamara and Travis Etienne split as driven by game flow rather than a set plan, and said CJ Donaldson was excellent in pass protection on third downs. Martin Emerson Jr. left with a shoulder injury that is day to day, and Moore said the team is otherwise relatively clean apart from bumps and bruises. The Saints now play several games at home, starting with Week 3 against the Raiders.

title: Aaron Glenn Press Conference (9/21) | Week 3
headline: Glenn vows to get Garrett Wilson more involved after a quiet second half, but the run game struggled against Green Bay's interior and injury updates won't come until Wednesday.
summary: Glenn said he will have a fuller injury update on Wednesday for the players he discussed after the game. He called the loss disappointing but said he was encouraged that the Jets dictated play until about eight minutes into the fourth quarter, and he took responsibility for not closing the door. He defended his late-game choices, including going for it on fourth-and-one at the logo and not calling a timeout at 11 seconds, and said the punt return touchdown and the failed fourth down were bigger swing plays. He said the run game struggled mainly because of Green Bay's interior pressure, though the Jets found some success on perimeter runs, with Breece Hall getting a couple and Braelon Allen breaking a touchdown. He said Geno Smith was distributing the ball fairly well in the passing game. Asked about Garrett Wilson being targeted only twice in the second half, he called getting Wilson the ball a point of emphasis and also named Breece Hall and Mason Taylor as players to keep involved. He said special teams were hurt by injuries that forced starters into extra roles, and he praised the safety play for keeping a roof over Green Bay's deep passing game. The next opponent is Detroit, which he called a tough game.

injuries.detail: Glenn said he will have a better update on Wednesday on the players he discussed after the game; no specifics were given in this session.

signals.claim: Wilson will be a point of emphasis and will get more targets going forward.
signals.note: A WR1 who faded after halftime, with the coach explicitly promising more looks, is a buy-low spot, especially against Detroit.

signals.note: His efficiency depends on whether the line can handle interior pressure, but the coach lists him among the players to get involved.

signals.note: The coach named him in the list of players to get the ball, a mildly positive target-share signal for a TE.
He broke a touchdown run, which shows his backfield role still has some weight, though the coach did not discuss his workload.
signals.quote: I thought Braylon broke one. That was one for the touchdown.

signals.quote: I still thought that Geno was dealing the ball in the passing game fairly well.

topics.detail: Glenn defended not calling a timeout in the final minute, saying he did not want a backed-up offense with Green Bay holding two timeouts, and said the Jets planned to play for overtime. He does not regret going for it on fourth-and-one.
Green Bay's interior defenders were the main problem, and the Jets need other options when teams take away their strength. Perimeter runs worked better.
The Jets forced five fumbles but recovered only one. Glenn called it bad bounces and was glad the defense is attacking the ball.
Injuries forced starters into special teams roles, and Glenn said he will not use that as an excuse. He was pleased with the safeties for limiting Green Bay's deep passes.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: September 21, 2026
headline: Dallas Goedert's knee and Saquon Barkley's MRI status are both unresolved. Tank Bigsby got a touchdown and praise after Barkley got banged up, and the run game is still 'close' but not producing.
summary: Sirianni praised Cam Jurgens for moving from center to left guard on short notice against a good Titans front. Jurgens had few reps there beforehand, but he got a lot during the week and played a solid game. On the running game, Sirianni called it a full-team effort across coaches, backs, line, tight ends, receivers and the quarterback. He said the Eagles are close to creating explosives, are still committed to running, and have room to improve. He gave no update on Saquon Barkley beyond saying it was early in the day and he'd check with the medical staff later, with the week to unfold. On Dallas Goedert, he said they were still waiting on information about the knee and wouldn't speculate. He said he likes the tight end room even though Eli Stowers is also out and the group is banged up. He had high praise for Tank Bigsby, citing a drive down to the 3-yard line, a touchdown, and a special-teams tackle on a punt. He credited Jalen Hurts' improved work to the backside and middle of the field to his commitment to improving, his accumulated reps as a six-year starter, and partly new backside route concepts in the new scheme. He declined to explain why the roster spot stayed open, deferring to Howie and saying they'd see by the end of the week.

title: WATCH: McCarthy Previews Week 3 against Bengals
headline: Michael Pittman (new foot injury) is a true unknown for Week 3, while McCarthy blames the offense's early struggles on protection and an overloaded game plan, not on Aaron Rodgers.
summary: McCarthy said the offense must clean up its own mistakes after a slow start and a second straight week of failed third downs. He pointed to pass protection and man-to-man coverage as the main problems. He took responsibility for too much play volume, saying he leaned on Rodgers' experience too heavily and wants less volume with more creativity. The offensive line needs continuity and more reps together, since the five starters have rarely practiced at the same time. He said Rodgers was hit too much, called the team a 'protection first' unit, and said he is not worried about how Rodgers responds. Michael Pittman has a different foot injury from the one in camp and goes into the Wednesday evaluation group, with no read on his availability. McCarthy praised Max Iheanachor's weekly progress, and said Troy Fautanu and Mason McCormick have handled the move from right to left well. He previewed the Bengals, calling Dexter Lawrence a challenge, and said Joe Burrow (back flare-up) is in the Wednesday work-up group, so his status is unclear.

The offense had manageable third downs and did not convert them for a second straight week. McCarthy cited pass protection issues and man-to-man coverage, including free runners from technique errors.
He called Dexter Lawrence a challenge he knows from his Dallas days and said the Bengals have an outstanding offense. Division game, with the staff beginning prep Wednesday.
He said drops are handled by building confidence and finding ways to get receivers the ball earlier in games, with no individual named.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Recaps Week 2, Gives Injury Updates
headline: Drew Lock is likely to start again while Sam Darnold's Wednesday practice status is unclear. Emanuel Wilson impressed as a downhill runner, and Charbonnet's return timeline is still open.
summary: Macdonald called Seattle's run defense a good early-season stat but said he could have adjusted the front structures better against Arizona. He said the defense is trying to generate more pressure and is more focused than in his first two years. Drew Lock got heavy praise for his first start, including his handling of pressure and protection. With Sam Darnold's situation 'up in the air', the week's preparation will be handled differently. Darnold's plan is to be on the practice field in some capacity by Wednesday. Zach Charbonnet's return timeline is still being worked out around how much practice time he needs. The offensive line rotated Christian Haynes and Beau Stephens because Abraham Lucas couldn't go, and Lucas will be monitored going forward. Emanuel Wilson drew praise for decisive, downhill running, while Jadarian Price has a minor issue Macdonald said shouldn't be long term. Nick Emmanwori came through the game well and will have his reps managed this week. Macdonald also said defenses can double Jaxon Smith-Njigba in two ways but not three, so Seattle will keep moving him around.

title: Shanahan Reacts to 49ers 35-13 Win Over Dolphins, Talks Purdy's Growth
headline: 49ers won 35-13 and Purdy was sharp, but Mike Evans (hip) and Demarcus Robinson (likely high ankle sprain) were hurt, and a WR addition is expected by Wednesday.
summary: Shanahan was pleased with the 35-13 win and the team's focus after the long trip and travel. He called Brock Purdy sharp and on point, with one incompletion a drop and another a third-down bust. He said the bootleg and keeper game worked well and produced throws and scramble yards. George Kittle scored for the first time since returning from injury, on a third-quarter play where a double corner blitz opened the middle. Christian McCaffrey reached 100 career touchdowns. Shanahan said Miami controlled the clock early, and the defense kept them out of the end zone until late. He still thinks the run defense gave up too many big plays and needs to improve. The receiver room is thin: Demarcus Robinson went down in this game, other receivers were lost earlier, and Christian Kirk is a couple of weeks away. Shanahan expects to add a receiver from the practice squad or outside the building, with an answer hopefully by Wednesday, and he ruled out Brandon Aiyuk. The defensive line is also depleted, and the team has talked to veteran Leonard Floyd.

title: Todd Bowles on Getting it Right: Capitalizing | Press Conference
headline: Bucky Irving is the lead back with the hot hand, while Jalen McMillan (9 snaps, no targets) is close to healthy and will get a bigger role; Bowles says Kenny Gainwell remains a '1B' and the Bucs are 0-2.
summary: Bowles said the Bucs are 0-2 after a loss to Cleveland, and that the offense has to make plays and execute better, including in two-minute situations. On defense, a late scoring drive came down to missed tackles, a 15-yard face mask penalty, and a few third-down opportunities they let slip. He stayed confident in Alex Anzalone despite his early struggles, saying many players have things to clean up and he won't bench people for mistakes. Rookie Rueben Bain isn't completely healthy after his AC sprain but is good enough to play, and Bowles wants more production from him. The offensive line is still working on cohesion, with the run game going well but pass protection and stunt pickup needing work, and holding penalties tied to Baker Mayfield's scrambling. Teams are packing the middle of the field, so Tampa Bay will lean on the run and more outside concepts. Jalen McMillan, back from injury, is close to fully healthy and will have a bigger role once he is. Bowles defended Bucky Irving's 17-carry workload and said Kenny Gainwell, Sean Tucker and possibly Josh Williams will all be needed. Next up is Minnesota, where they must prepare for both Murray and Wentz at QB plus Justin Jefferson and a pressure-heavy defense.

Bowles described the locker room as 'angrily optimistic' and said there's urgency to get the first win.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Cordale Flott's ankle/availability for the Giants is in doubt after he missed Week 2, and rookies Elic Ayomanor, Carnell Tate and Nicholas Singleton drew praise after a late-game loss to the Eagles.
summary: Saleh called the loss exactly as sickening as expected on film. He blamed the late breakdowns on all three phases, from the first-and-goal at the nine on, and said the play callers could have put the team in better spots. He defended settling for field goals at the end of the half and the end of the game as a feel-for-the-game decision. He said he would be more aggressive if the team were further along, but he didn't want to put the ball in harm's way while the defense was playing well. He explained the time-of-possession gap by saying the Eagles crushed Tennessee on third down in the first half, when the pass rush and coverage execution were off. He called the offensive line good and much improved, but said it still needs more consistency. He liked the young group, singling out Elic Ayomanor for his work ethic and run-game effort and saying Carnell Tate and Gunnar Helm are taking good steps. Rookie back Nicholas Singleton got a few carries and left some yardage out there. Cordale Flott got worse after being limited Thursday and missed the game. Saleh hopes to have him back at practice Wednesday ahead of the Giants.

injuries.detail: Something was bothering him Thursday and he was rested Friday, but it kept getting worse and he missed Sunday. Saleh hopes he is back at practice Wednesday for the Giants.

signals.claim: Will keep growing into a bigger role in the receiver rotation

signals.quote: I love his mindset. I love his work ethic.

signals.note: Coach is encouraged by the rookie's development and effort, which supports his snap and target outlook.
signals.quote: I thought Carnell took a couple of good steps.

signals.note: He is only a change-of-pace option for now, with a long-term upside Saleh likes but little current volume.
signals.quote: I think he's going to be a really good back in this league.

signals.note: A niche role tied to three-tight-end looks, so there is little fantasy value unless the backfield changes.
signals.quote: does a really nice job with teams dressed in three tight ends

signals.claim: Hopes to get him back in practice Wednesday and ready for the Giants
signals.note: His availability for the Giants is uncertain, which affects the Titans' secondary depth.
signals.quote: it just kept going downhill from there.

signals.claim: Will keep playing outside corner full time rather than moving between corner and nickel
signals.note: Saleh described early bumps as normal adjustment, so this mainly matters for IDP formats.
signals.quote: I like where he's, where he's trending.

signals.claim: Is earning ongoing tight end playing time
signals.note: Coach praised him by name among the young offensive players, a mild positive for his role.
signals.quote: Gunner helm is doing a really nice job.

signals.note: Saleh said Ward took a step forward but also wished he had given Ayomanor a better ball on one end-zone throw.
signals.quote: cam took a nice step stepped yesterday

signals.claim: Should have sealed the inside on the failed first-and-goal play from the nine
signals.note: He lost a key rep against Jalen Carter, though Saleh gave much of the credit to Carter.
signals.quote: you'd love for us for JC to seal him on the inside

topics.detail: Saleh said settling for field goals at the end of the half and the end of the game was based on feel, not philosophy. He called going more aggressive on second-and-goal from the 18 a toss-up, and said he would be more aggressive once the team has grown.

He blamed first-half third-down failures, a weak pass rush and loose coverage for the Eagles' long drives, and said the second half was more balanced. Week 1's imbalance was credited to the Jets staying ahead of the chains.
He rated the line good and much improved from Week 1, with two penalties and Jalen Carter's play on first-and-goal as the lapses. He still wants more consistency.
The Eagles' last touchdown came against zero coverage, and Saleh said the corners failed to recognize it and squeeze. He called it an execution failure.
Saleh said the young team has to trust its process and not let the losing streak snowball, and that it is still learning how to win close games.
Saleh assumed the water sprayed on cleats was a response to the heat, and said he had never seen it done before.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 09/21/26
headline: Jayden Daniels re-injured his elbow and will see specialists Tue/Wed, with no timeline; Marcus Mariota starts Sunday at home, and Cosmi is in concussion protocol.
summary: Quinn opened by saying Jayden Daniels had imaging done and will see specialists early this week, so he would not guess at a timeline. Marcus Mariota will start Sunday, and Quinn praised him as one of the team's top leaders. Daniels' injury was described as a freak play in which he was stepped on at the line on a keep-or-toss option, and Quinn said there was no discussion of surgery last year because it was part of the rehab plan. Quinn expects to update on Daniels around Thursday or Friday, and said he has not yet discussed signing another veteran QB with the GM. Nick Cross was evaluated for an internal injury, stayed overnight in Dallas, was discharged and is flying back, with an update expected Wednesday. Brandon Coleman (finger) looks good to go, Javon Kinlaw (shoulder) will be limited early in the week pending imaging, and Samuel Cosmi has entered concussion protocol. Quinn was unhappy with the secondary's communication and urgency after four touchdown passes allowed (including on the premium receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens), and said the defense needs more takeaways but is getting closer. The team is 0-2 heading into the home opener and is described as resolute.

injuries.detail: Re-injured elbow (third elbow issue; dislocation per reporters, no fractures per earlier report). Imaging done; specialists Tue/Wed; no timeline; update likely Thu/Fri.
Internal injury, stayed overnight in Dallas, discharged and flying back; update expected Wednesday.

signals.note: Internal injury that required a hospital stay makes his availability uncertain, which matters for IDP.

topics.detail: Quinn said he and the GM had not discussed bringing in another veteran QB and would wait for info over the next two days.
Quinn said no playbook pullback is needed for Mariota, who is familiar with the system; the offense will be similar but with different features.
Quinn criticized communication, urgency and the handling of the premium receivers after four TD passes allowed to Dallas, including a seam-route touchdown to a tight end similar to the week before.
Quinn liked the run defense and the pressure, but the team has no takeaways in two games. He cited Daron Payne's and K'Lavon Chaisson's shots at the ball, and Odafe Oweh's good play.
The team is 0-2 but resolute, and excited for the home opener after a long stretch away from home.
